explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.02% of steps). About 42% of activation mass is at t=2 (the third original token) when the first two tokens are both z or f (zz, zf, fz, ff) and the current token is one of e,h,r,o,a,2,u,j,x. It stays silent for other third tokens such as digits 3, l, q, v, k. Precision on this clause is about 0.6. Another ~40% of the mass is at the copy step right after <DEL>, where the model re-inputs orig(0) and outputs orig(1). This is strongest when orig(0)=e and the sequence is long (L>=7) and contains z, and it includes the top activations (e.g. e ... <DEL> [e]). No simple predicate captures that clause with useful precision (best ~0.06), so it is left out. Small activations also occur at the <DEL> step and at t=3/4 after z/f runs. It never fires at t=0,1 or at recall_idx>=2. Magnitude claims are not checked beyond the top examples, which are dominated by the post-<DEL> e echo.
